summary: The root "srmd" signifies continuous, unending time, whether day or night. It describes something perpetual or everlasting, like an endless night.
lane: سَرْمَدٌ ذ [signifies, or implies,] Continuance, or incessant continuance, ( دَوَام , Kh, M, L, and اِتِّصَال , Kh, L,) of time, (Kh, M, L,) either of night or of day. (Kh, L.) [I have said “ or implies ” because I have not found it used otherwise than as an epithet, in the following senses.] -b2- Continuing; or continuing incessantly, or endlessly; syn. دَائِمٌ ; (Zj, S, L, K;) or دَائِمٌ لَا يَنْقَطِعُ . (Nh, L.) It is applied in this sense to night (Nh, L) [and also to day: to each in the Kur xxviii. 71 and 72]: and to night as meaning Long. (L, K.) -b3- Accord. to El-Fakhr Er-Rázee, it is derived from السَّرْدُ , which denotes consecutiveness and uninterruptedness, and the م is added to give intensiveness to the signification: if so, its proper place is in art. سرد ; its measure being فَعْمَلٌ : (MF:) [thus] its م is augmentative like the م in دُلَامِصٌ . (Bd in xxviii. 71.) -b4- One says also, هُوَ لَكَ سَرْمَدًا He, or it, is thine ever, or for ever. (Mgh in art. سمد .)

entries.text: السرمد: دوام الزمان من ليل ونهار. والسرمد: دوام العيش.
(السَّرْمَدُ) : الدَّائِمُ، وَالْمِيمُ فِيهِ زَائِدَةٌ، وَهُوَ مِنْ سَرَدَ، إِذَا وَصَلَ، فَكَأَنَّهُ زَمَانٌ مُتَّصِلٌ بَعْضُهُ بِبَعْضٍ. وَمِنْ ذَلِكَ
السَّرْمَدُ: الدّائم، قال تعالى: ﴿قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكُمُ اللَّيْلَ سَرْمَداً﴾ [القصص : 71] ، وبعده: ﴿النَّهارَ سَرْمَداً﴾ [القصص : 72] .

سرمد: السرْمَدُ: دَوَامُ الزَّمَانِ مِنْ لَيْلٍ أَو نَهَارٍ. وَلَيْلٌ سَرْمَدٌ: طَوِيلٌ. وَفِي التَّنْزِيلِ الْعَزِيزِ: قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكُمُ النَّهارَ سَرْمَداً ؟ قَالَ الزَّجَّاجُ: السَّرْمَدُ الدَّائِمُ فِي اللُّغَةِ. وَفِي حَدِيثِ لُقْمَانَ: جَوّابُ لَيْلٍ سَرْمَد؛ السَّرْمَدُ: الدَّائِمُ الَّذِي لَا يَنْقَطِعُ.

السَّرْمَدُ : الدَّائِمُ الَّذي لا ينقطع قُلْ أَرَأَيتُمْ إِنْ جَعَلَ اللَّهُ عَلَيكُمُ اللَّيْلَ سَرْمَداً إلَى يوْمِ القِيَامَةِ.-: هو في الفلسفة، ما لا أَوَّلَ له ولا آخر، فهو خارج عن مقولة الزمان وموجودٌ بلا بدءٍ ولا نهاية.

classical_note: Arabic-only entries from public-domain classical lexica, ordered by compiler death date. Tier 'root-semantic' (Maqayis) derives all senses of a root from one core idea. Tier 'interpretive' (Mufradat) cites hadith and takes theological positions and is not equivalent evidence. Tier 'earliest-disputed' (Kitab al-Ayn) marks a text whose attribution to al-Khalil ibn Ahmad (d. 786) is contested: the work itself records that his student al-Layth ibn al-Muzaffar completed it after his death, so the 786 date orders the entry but does not assert sole authorship. Kitab al-Ayn is arranged by point of articulation, not alphabetically, and files geminate roots with two letters; the al-Ayn headword actually used is preserved in each entry.
